name: Lithium-plating aging study: C/2 charge / D/2 discharge cycling of NCA/SiOx-graphite 18650 cells at -10 C versus 25 C with ICA/DVA/EIS check-ups and post-mortem validation
plain_name: Charge and discharge battery cells over and over at -10 C to see metal lithium build up
description: Commercial Sanyo NCR 18650GA cells (3.35 Ah, 2.5-4.2 V) are cycled at C/2 charge and D/2 discharge at -10 C (to promote lithium plating) and at 25 C (baseline), three cells per condition, with check-ups every 100 cycles to 80 % SoH and post-mortem CT/SEM/XRD/7Li NMR; motivated by fast, safe charging for electrified transportation.
keywords: Charge and discharge battery cells over and over at -10 C to see metal lithium build up

sources.citation: Herran A. et al., Advanced Electrochemical Diagnostics Validation for Early Detection of Lithium Plating in Lithium-Ion Batteries, ACS Omega (2026), doi:10.1021/acsomega.5c06081, PMC13150617

requirements.rationale: Aging temperature -10 C (263.15 K) chosen to promote lithium plating.
Baseline aging and check-up temperature 25 C (298.15 K).
Cells are continuously charged and discharged by a battery cycler while at temperature.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
